mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of quarters where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where UNRATE is below 5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods where INDPRO is below its 12-month MA for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual monetary tightening and inflationary pressure, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month MA
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods where both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL are above their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages for two consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both above 12-month MA for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods where both PAYEMS and RSAFS are above their 12-month moving averages for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals a deepening labor market slack, which reduces wage growth and corporate cost pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as profit margins expand.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods where UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a recovery in residential construction activity, which boosts demand for materials and labor and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods where HOUST is above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months.
